input.answer: Consumer prices were rising at 3.1% a year in September 2026. Canada's all-items CPI (not seasonally adjusted) was 170.0 in September 2026, up from 164.9 in September 2025. The change is (170.0 − 164.9) / 164.9 = 5.1 / 164.9 = 3.09%, which rounds to 3.1%. The change in index points is +5.1. I read "a year earlier" as September 2025. The September 2026 data point is the latest in the table (its range runs to 2026-09). Source: Statistics Canada Table 18-10-0004-01, Consumer Price Index, monthly, not seasonally adjusted (Canada, All-items, vector 41690973).
